title: The hidden cost of the quick question

sections.title: A whole morning
sections.role: how it works, why it matters

narration: Say you are deep in a plan.
It takes a minute to answer.
is the plan where you left it?
beats.visual_intent: an editorial page: one piece of work, the plan, sits half written in a held slot at the centre; a small paper slip slides in at the edge carrying Quick question?; it is answered, and the page's time strip runs on to lunch while the plan stays exactly as it was

grounding.claim: the worker, the plan, the message and the one-minute answer are an invented, typical example

narration: The minute is the visible part.
and what a team can do.
beats.visual_intent: a two-column ledger is ruled onto the page beside the slot, headed visible and hidden; one small accent unit drops into visible on minute, the hidden column stays empty and waiting

grounding.claim: an interruption costs more than the time spent answering it

narration: To answer, you put the plan down.
and make more mistakes after a switch.
beats.visual_intent: the held slot swaps: the plan slides out and the question slides in; on switch cost, the first unit is stamped into the hidden column and lettered; the visible column is unchanged

grounding.claim: after a switch people are slower and make more errors than when repeating the same task (laboratory finding)

narration: Then you come back, but not really.
You hunt for where you were.
beats.visual_intent: the plan slides back into the slot greyed and out of register; a small search mark moves over its lines until it finds where you were; a second, longer unit is stamped into the hidden column, lettered resumption lag

grounding.claim: after an interruption there is a delay before a person is productive again while they work out where they were, called the resumption lag

narration: And part of your mind stays on the question.
The next thing you do suffers.
beats.visual_intent: a faint ghost of the message slip stays printed over the corner of the plan; a third, pale unit is stamped into the hidden column, lettered attention residue

grounding.claim: after switching away from an unfinished task, part of attention tends to stay on it and performance on the next task tends to be worse

beats.misconception: I can answer while still writing, so there is no switch
narration: and every switch goes in the hidden column.
beats.visual_intent: the slot flickers between the plan and the message several times, never holding both; each flick stamps a small unit into the hidden column

grounding.claim: for two demanding tasks, what feels like multitasking is mostly rapid switching, and each switch carries a cost

beats.visual_intent: the finished ledger for one question rests: one small unit under visible, the stamped units under hidden; the two column heads take the accent in turn

recall.prompt: Keep the two columns in mind: visible and hidden. Watch which one grows.

grounding.claim: the cost has a visible part (answering) and a hidden part (switching and getting back in)
the sizes of the units on the ledger are illustrative

narration: Say five questions, a minute each,
and a few more to get back in.
beats.visual_intent: the page becomes the morning as a grid of time units; the first question stamps one accent unit and, beside it, a short run of ink units for getting back in; a small margin note reads varies

grounding.claim: five questions, a minute each and a few more to get back in, are illustrative sizes
there is no single reliable figure for recovery time; it varies

narration: Visible, one unit. Hidden, a run.
beats.visual_intent: the stamps speed up question by question, each one accent unit followed by its ink run; the grid fills from the top while the plan's own units, the real work, barely advance

grounding.claim: the morning's questions and their unit counts are illustrative

narration: found work fragmented, much like this.
beats.visual_intent: the same grid: the plan's units now sit scattered in small pieces between the question runs, none of them joined

grounding.claim: field observation found office information workers' work highly fragmented, with frequent switching

beats.misconception: if I answer fast and catch up, the cost disappears
narration: Going faster does not fix it.
In one experiment, people sped up,
beats.visual_intent: the hidden runs compress as the worker races, but their stamps relabel one by one from time to stress; the hidden column keeps its height

grounding.claim: in one experiment, interrupted people worked faster but reported more stress, frustration and effort

narration: For the asker, it is one small message,
The hidden column lands on someone else.
Nobody is careless. Now is just the default.
beats.visual_intent: the spread turns like a magazine page: on the left the asker's page holds one small accent unit and their work moves a step on unstuck; on the right the interrupted page holds the whole hidden pile; a thin line carries the message across

grounding.claim: interrupting a colleague often helped the asker get unstuck quickly, while the cost fell on the person interrupted
questions between colleagues are often valuable

beats.visual_intent: the morning grid with all five slips gathered at one slot at its edge; both column heads, visible and hidden, carry a question mark; nothing moves through the pause

recall.prompt: If the same questions arrived together at one agreed time, which column shrinks: visible or hidden?
recall.answer: hidden: the answers take the same minutes, but there is one switch and one return instead of one for every question
recall.tempting_wrong: visible: it feels like fewer interruptions means less answering, but the answering is the same; only the switching is saved

grounding.claim: the batching scenario is illustrative

narration: But one switch, and one return.
beats.visual_intent: the five slips slide into one batch slot; the visible units stay exactly as they were; the five hidden runs collapse into a single run and the plan's scattered units rejoin into one long block; each slip gets a small tick as answered
beats.misconception: the fix is to ask fewer questions

grounding.claim: sending questions together reduces how often the other person has to switch
the aim is to change when non-urgent questions arrive, not to stop asking them
the unit sizes are illustrative

beats.visual_intent: the morning layout becomes the habits' board; a first label, batch, pins to the batch slot on its word, and agreed times marks two set points on the time strip

grounding.claim: collecting non-urgent questions and sending them together reduces switching
teams agree how quickly non-urgent messages are answered so they can be answered in batches
checking messages at set times was linked to less stress in one study

narration: with a route for the truly urgent.
Then the habit faded. Keep it up.
beats.visual_intent: a block of the morning grid is shaded as focus time with a narrow open lane at its edge for urgent; the shading thins on faded, then is re-inked on keep it up

grounding.claim: teams agree which channel means urgent
in one team's trial of quiet periods many reported better productivity, and the habit faded after the trial ended

narration: note where you are, and what comes next.
In experiments, that cut attention residue.
beats.visual_intent: callback to b04: before the plan leaves the slot, a small note is clipped to it reading where you are and what comes next; the ghost of the message over the plan fades on residue

grounding.claim: a brief ready-to-resume note before switching reduced attention residue in experiments

narration: Same questions, held for the agreed time.
By lunch, the plan has moved.
beats.visual_intent: the hook's page returns from the same angle: the slips stack in the batch slot, the hidden column holds one short run, and the plan in the held slot is now visibly further written

recall.prompt: Each habit shrinks the hidden column, never the visible one.

grounding.claim: the returned morning is the illustrative example handled with the habits

narration: does it need an answer now?
And take one habit to your team.
beats.visual_intent: a new slip, Quick question?, hovers at the edge of the page; on batch it the slip settles into the batch slot instead of the held slot, and the plan stays in place

grounding.claim: non-urgent questions can be held and sent together; urgent ones are still asked at once
a team can agree habits such as response times and an urgent route
